memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The descendants of Jacob numbered seventy in all; Joseph was already in Egypt. Now Joseph and all his brothers and all that generation died," - Exodus 1:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Seventy people. That is all Israel was at the start. And then, quietly, a whole generation dies — Joseph, the great man who saved Egypt from famine, and all his brothers with him.

There is something sobering here. Joseph had been second only to Pharaoh. He had wisdom, position, and influence. Yet his chapter closed like every human chapter closes. The Bible does not hide this. It simply records it and moves on, because the story was never really about Joseph. It was about the God who is still working after Joseph is gone.

We often tie our hope to people — a godly parent, a faithful pastor, a leader who seemed irreplaceable. When they pass on, it can feel as if God's work has stalled. It has not. Generations rise and fall, but God's purposes continue unbroken.

This is exactly why Scripture points us to Jesus, the priest who lives forever and never needs replacing (Heb 7:23-25). Every human helper is temporary. He is not.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Whose faith am I depending on instead of building my own?
2. What am I doing today that will outlast my lifetime?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, my life is short but You are eternal. Teach me to number my days and to build on Christ, who never dies. Amen.
